reasoning_content:
Let me examine the QGIS MAP issue. The guide says QGIS Server: `https://qgis.localhost/ows/?MAP=/projects/<project>.qgs`. The test-project.qgz is a 16-byte placeholder provided by user, not a valid project. So the 500 is expected due to no valid project file — that's a data issue, not installation. But is the QGIS server operational? The healthcheck passes with a plain GetCapabilities at "/" returning 615 bytes. Let me check the direct qgis server root.

Actually the healthcheck hitting `/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities` returns 200 at port 80 inside container. Let me test that path through caddy without MAP. We got 500 with MAP and without MAP through /ows/. But the healthcheck hits "/" not "/ows/". Let's test `https://qgis.localhost/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities`.

Also the tiles data endpoint. Let me check tileserver config.json to understand.

Let me also verify the frontend actually talks to backend correctly. But main concern: is installation "operational according to the guide". The guide primarily documents Docker Compose services. The installation summary says incomplete/unknown QGIS projects (only placeholder) and tiles only Monaco.

Let me check the tileserver root content and config.

action.command:
cd /workspace/deployment
echo "=== tileserver config ==="; cat tiles/config.json
echo "=== tiles data dir ==="; find tiles/data -maxdepth 3 | head
echo "=== tileserver root ==="; curl -sk --resolve tiles.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 https://tiles.localhost/ | head -c 600
echo; echo "=== tiles style ==="; curl -sk --resolve tiles.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -o /dev/null -w "styles:%{http_code}\n" https://tiles.localhost/styles/basic/style.json
echo "=== qgis root (no /ows) ==="; curl -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 "https://qgis.localhost/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities" -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}\n" | head -c 400
